record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Is every orbit equivalence relation arising from a Borel action of a countable amenable group hyperfinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 40 (Weiss’ question). Is the orbit equivalence relation of Borel action of countable amenable group hyperfinite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Borel equivalence relation on a standard Borel space $X$ is a subset $E \subseteq X \times X$ that is an equivalence relation and is Borel as a subset of $X \times X$. Such an $E$ is called countable if every $E$-equivalence class is countable. A countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ on $X$ is called hyperfinite if there is an increasing sequence $E_0 \subseteq E_1 \subseteq E_2 \subseteq \cdots$ of Borel equivalence relations on $X$ such that each $E_n$ has all classes finite and $E = \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} E_n$.

A countable discrete group $G$ is amenable if there exists a finitely additive, left-invariant probability measure on the power set of $G$ (equivalently, $G$ admits a F\o lner sequence). A Borel action of $G$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is an action $G \times X \to X$ that is Borel as a function, and its orbit equivalence relation $E_G^X$ is defined by $x \, E_G^X \, y \iff \exists g \in G\; g \cdot x = y$; this $E_G^X$ is a countable Borel equivalence relation.

Question: Is it true that for every countable amenable group $G$ and every Borel action of $G$ on a standard Borel space $X$, the orbit equivalence relation $E_G^X$ is hyperfinite?
artifact.status_search_result: Weiss's question remains open in full generality. It has been resolved positively for many classes of countable amenable groups: abelian groups (Gao–Jackson), polycyclic groups, locally nilpotent groups, and more recently (via Borel asymptotic dimension techniques of Conley–Jackson–Marks–Seward–Tucker-Drob and others) for all virtually polycyclic groups, lamplighter-type groups, and virtually solvable groups of finite Prüfer rank. The general case for arbitrary countable amenable groups is still unresolved as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Borel asymptotic dimension and hyperfinite equivalence relations
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes hyperfiniteness for orbit equivalence relations of Borel actions of polycyclic groups and other classes, addressing partial cases of Weiss's question.
status_evidence.claim: Weiss's question is resolved for polycyclic groups and several further classes of amenable groups.

status_evidence.title: Hyper-u-amenability and Hyperfiniteness of Treeable Equivalence Relations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Weiss's question as a long-standing open problem and proves further partial results extending known hyperfinite classes.
status_evidence.claim: The general Weiss question remains open as of 2025, with new partial results continuing to appear.
